$comment: THE SINGLE DECLARATION of every version the build depends on. [pipeline F-2]
GitHub Actions has no native shared constant across workflows, so these values
are still WRITTEN in each workflow — what this file buys is that they can no
longer DRIFT: tooling/ci/assert-version-consistency.mjs fails the build naming
the file and line of any literal that disagrees with the values here.
So: declared once, enforced everywhere — not written literally once. Changing a
version means editing this file and the call sites; the guard tells you exactly
which one you forgot, instead of one lane silently building on a different SDK.
Before this existed, '3.44.7' appeared in SIX places and 'node-version: 24' in
EIGHT, and tooling/wsl-setup.sh carried the comment 'keep in lockstep with
*.yml' — a maintenance instruction addressed to a human, which is exactly the
mechanism this repo keeps finding does not hold.
mason_cli was pinned NOWHERE: `dart pub global activate mason_cli` took the
newest release on every run. Mason is what STAMPS APPS, so an unpinned mason
means the factory's actual product could differ between runs with nothing in
the repo to explain it. That was the sharpest item on the list.

$runners_comment: PINNED — owner decision 2026-07-26. Previously all 17 `runs-on:` values were
'-latest', which carries the same hazard as a floating action tag: macos-latest
rolling to a new Xcode changes what an identical commit builds, with no diff in
the repo at all.
Why pinning helps here: '-latest' rolls to a whole new OS image unannounced in
your repo, while a pinned label at least fails loudly when the image is finally
retired. That is the same principle every other guard in tooling/ci serves.
🔴 CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — this used to claim a pinned image 'fails LOUDLY and ON
A SCHEDULE' while '-latest' fails 'SILENTLY and UNSCHEDULED'. That overstates it,
and GitHub's own changelog is the counter-example:
https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-14-github-actions-upcoming-image-migrations/
'The `windows-latest` AND `windows-2025` labels in GitHub Actions will be
migrated to use Visual Studio 2026 by default.'  (rolled out 8-15 June 2026;
`windows-2022` is the way to stay on VS 2022.)
So our Windows lane changed COMPILERS under an unchanged pin, silently, with no
diff in this repo — exactly the failure the original wording promised pinning
prevented. PINNING A RUNNER LABEL NARROWS THE DRIFT; IT DOES NOT REMOVE IT.
A label names an image family, not an immutable image.
Kept anyway: narrower drift is still worth having, and the alternative ('-latest')
drifts across OS major versions rather than tool versions. But do not read these
pins as a guarantee of a reproducible toolchain — they are not one.
Cost, stated plainly: images are eventually retired and CI then breaks hard
rather than drifting. These land in the SAME maintenance bucket as the F-11
action pins, so one mechanism — Renovate, stage 14 — covers both.
Labels verified against actions/runner-images README before pinning, not
guessed: a wrong label yields 'no runner matching the labels' and the job never
starts. Current aliases: ubuntu-latest→24.04, windows-latest→2025, macos-latest
→macOS 26 Arm64.
$wrangler_comment: ADDED 2026-07-28 after the external-facts pass found the worst kind of drift:
the tool that PUBLISHES production was not on this list at all.
cloudflare/wrangler-action runs `npm i wrangler@<version>`. It resolves that
version from the package.json in `workingDirectory` — and deploy-web.yml points
it at `apps/subly`, which is a Flutter app with NO package.json. So the action
fell back to the constant compiled into its own bundle: 3.90.0.
`npm i wrangler@3.90.0` while both Workers lock 4.114.0. A MAJOR version behind
the rest of the repo, past its bug-fix window per Cloudflare's own changelog,
holding the account API token, and chosen by a third party's default.
F-2 says every version is declared once and F-11 says build inputs are pinned.
Both read VERIFIED while this was true, because both looked at what the repo
WRITES and never at what the deploy RESOLVES.
